definition: The collective delusion that owning a fractional claim on the global compute network makes you a stakeholder in civilization. Street term for the political fiction that the UBC represents meaningful participation in the economy.
origin: Shelf Cant — from 'cope,' the act of convincing yourself something bad is actually fine
example: They call it ownership. We call it Q-cope. I own one ten-billionth of the machine that decides whether I eat.
